trajectories.title: Sovereign accumulation
trajectories.thesis: Imported infrastructure becomes durable UAE capability through local operation, evaluation capacity, knowledge transfer, and credible replacement options.

horizon_blocks.programming_action: Microsoft investment and bilateral infrastructure finance allocate capital toward a UAE-based AI stack.
Chip authorization and campus capacity expand available frontier compute under continuing external conditions.
Operating and evaluating the stack may transfer durable expertise into UAE institutions.
Local evaluation and operating institutions could convert access into repeatable state capability.
Deployed AI systems may increase coordination and analytical capacity if locally governed and auditable.

indicators.observation: A UAE-governed institution independently evaluates deployed models and infrastructure against published methods.
indicators.supports_if: The institution can publish findings and require remediation without provider approval.

reversal_conditions: Core operation remains contractually or technically unavailable without a single foreign provider.
No transferable local evaluation or operating capability is observed by the review date.

trajectories.title: Managed interdependence
trajectories.thesis: The UAE gains substantial capability while external dependencies remain explicit, diversified, and governable through agreements and institutional bargaining power.

horizon_blocks.programming_action: Cross-border investment binds commercial incentives across the partnership.
Regulated access expands capacity while preserving supplier and export-control dependencies.
Bilateral principles, security conditions, and export permissions program the allowed operating space.
Assurance requirements align operation with a shared but externally influenced governance regime.
Technical, diplomatic, and commercial networks sustain bargaining and implementation across institutions.

indicators.observation: Public or auditable agreements establish continuity, portability, and replacement provisions across critical suppliers.
indicators.supports_if: Withdrawal of one provider does not terminate the core public capability.

reversal_conditions: Security or export conditions create unilateral interruption power without viable substitutes.
Provider diversification exists nominally but not operationally.

trajectories.title: Capability without control
trajectories.thesis: Operational capacity grows while chips, model access, assurance requirements, and key operating decisions remain externally controlled and difficult to replace.

horizon_blocks.programming_action: Foreign chip supply and authorization conditions concentrate interruption power outside the UAE.
Physical capacity grows locally while critical operation may remain tied to foreign platforms and suppliers.
Export and assurance regimes constrain which technologies and relationships remain permissible.
Local expertise may grow without acquiring authority over the upstream technical stack.
AI agents amplify capability but inherit access, policy, data, and compute constraints from the surrounding stack.

indicators.observation: A material capability interruption follows a foreign export, provider, or assurance-policy change.
indicators.supports_if: The UAE cannot restore equivalent operation through a pre-existing alternative within the stated continuity window.

reversal_conditions: Independent local operation and evaluation are demonstrated under a provider-change test.
Auditable multi-provider substitution materially reduces withdrawal exposure.
